name: status
description: Whether Basalt is ready for you, and what to do if not. Call it at the start of a session before any other Basalt tool, after the person says they fixed something (started the engine, ran an upgrade, registered a passkey), and after a failure that looks like setup rather than your statement (UNAVAILABLE, GUARD_OUTDATED, SETUP_PENDING). Answers even when the engine is down. Each problem carries nextSteps: do them in order, show the person personMessage verbatim and every PERSON step's command unchanged. When operatedBy is PERSON you never start, stop or upgrade anything yourself; when it is AGENT you run the machine steps addressed to you (AGENT RUN_COMMAND). In either case never ask the person for, or accept, their database admin connection string or password. Read-only; never returns a secret.

agent.description: This agent's name in the engine config.

operatedBy.description: Who runs the engine's machine (engine.json operatedBy). PERSON (default, and when the shim cannot read the config): machine steps are the person's. AGENT: machine steps are the agent's (AGENT RUN_COMMAND); steps that need the admin stay the person's, on their own computer.

enforcement.description: ENGINE_AND_GUARD: the engine runs as its own OS user and the agent cannot read its credential, so every statement passes the engine's checks and the guard's. GUARD_ONLY: operatedBy is AGENT, or the engine runs in same-user mode, or the shim cannot read the config: the agent could connect with its credential directly, and the guard in Postgres still enforces intent, row limits, holds and signatures.

ready.description: True when no problem has severity ERROR: every tool is served.

reachable.description: False when the shim answers because the engine socket does not.

build.description: The engine's build version; the shim's when the engine is down.

startedBy.description: Why this engine started: HAND (a person or a service manager ran it), MCP (basalt mcp found the engine down and started it) or CRASH (the supervisor restarted it after a crash). Reported by a running engine only.

lastStop.description: Reported by basalt mcp when the engine does not answer and its supervisor gave up restarting it (the problem ENGINE_GAVE_UP): why, and when. The problem message also says when the next try happens during the 1-minute hold-off after that give-up. Removed once an engine has stayed up for 10 seconds.

reason.description: The supervisor's reason; exit statuses and counts, never a secret.

state.description: OK: every migration of this build is installed. UPGRADE_AVAILABLE: only non-breaking migrations are missing; every tool is served. OUTDATED: a breaking migration is missing; every tool but status answers UNAVAILABLE reason GUARD_OUTDATED. NEWER: the guard is newer than this build (served). MISSING: no basalt_meta. UNKNOWN: the engine is down or the database cannot be reached.

build.description: The schema version this build installs.

setup.description: Setup from the person's laptop (basalt init --remote on the engine's machine, then basalt init --setup-code on the person's own computer), or from the connect page.

state.description: PENDING: a setup code was made and its setup is not recorded yet. For an INSTALL code every tool but status answers UNAVAILABLE reason SETUP_PENDING (problem SETUP_NOT_RUN); for an AGENT or UPGRADE code the tools keep working with what is installed (problem SETUP_CHANGE_PENDING; except a connect-only AGENT recovery code, served as a pending INSTALL). EXPIRED: an INSTALL code past expiresAt (reason and problem SETUP_EXPIRED); a new code is needed. An expired AGENT or UPGRADE code is dropped, and the problem that called for it comes back. DONE: no setup pending, and setupId names the agent's latest recorded setup. NONE: no setup pending and none recorded (set up with basalt init and the admin connection string), or the engine is down and no setup is pending. For a connect-only code (CONTRACT.md, Setup from your laptop, The engine and a connect-only code): PENDING also while the engine waits for the database's address; CONFIRM_DATABASE: the engine collected the address and probed it, and serves nothing until the person confirms the database (database names it; problem CONFIRM_DATABASE, and every tool but status and confirm_database answers UNAVAILABLE reason DATABASE_NOT_CONFIRMED); REFUSED: the person said it is not their database, the engine forgot the address and its password and recorded refused in engine.json, and a new code is needed (problem DATABASE_REFUSED).

setupId.description: PENDING and EXPIRED: the pending code's. DONE: the latest recorded setup's.

expiresAt.description: PENDING and EXPIRED: when the code expires or expired.

fingerprint.description: PENDING: the pending code's setup fingerprint. Tell the person to check that basalt init --setup-code shows the same one.

connectOnly.description: True when the pending code is connect-only: it has no target, the person pastes the database's connection string on the connect page, and the engine collects the address from the connect service. Absent otherwise.

database.description: CONFIRM_DATABASE: the database the engine collected and probed, which the agent names when it asks the person to confirm. Checked by the engine before it is shown: a host name of DNS characters, a port, a database name of letters, digits, _ . - up to 63 characters, and a Supabase ref of 20 lowercase letters and digits. Never a password.

served.description: Whether the engine serves the local approval and revert pages (short links).

url.description: The pages base URL links are built on.

vault.description: CONTRACT.md, Vault channel: the engine's connection to the hosted Vault and its identity. Absent when the engine is down.

state.description: OFF: engine.json vault is OFF, or pagesUrl is not the portal; short links use the local pages or long links. CONNECTING: dialling or authenticating. CONNECTED: authenticated (READY); portal short links work. UNREACHABLE: no READY for 30 seconds or more; the engine hands over long links and keeps retrying. KEY_ERROR: the key file is insecure, unreadable or invalid and was not replaced; long links until it is fixed or basalt engine rotate-key runs. Approvals work in every state.

engineId.description: The engine id (a fingerprint of its signing key), whenever the key file loads.

fingerprint.description: The engine id's first 16 characters in four groups, as the portal page shows it. The person compares the two.

registered.description: Whether at least one active passkey can approve held writes and sign reverts.

active.description: How many passkeys are active. Absent when the engine is down or the passkeys cannot be read.

keys.description: The active passkeys (at most 100), oldest first, each with its check code computed from the public key in the database. If the setup page showed a check code for the passkey it created, it is one of these: a passkey the person did not create means stop and remove it. Absent when none is active or the passkeys cannot be read.

checkCode.description: Five groups of four lowercase hex digits, from the first 10 bytes of sha256("basalt-passkey-check.1\n" || x || y) of the key's P-256 coordinates.

summary.description: How many passkeys are registered and the check code of each, in words for the person. Set once a setup is recorded (setup.state DONE) and at least one passkey is listed.

ledger.description: How much space the ledger takes and how long it is kept. Absent when the guard cannot be read.

bytes.description: The size of every table, index and TOAST table in basalt_meta, in bytes.

valuesKeptDays.description: Days a change's old and new values are kept before they are pruned (30).

recordsKeptDays.description: Days a ledger record is kept before it is deleted (365).

trust.description: What verifies the agent's database certificate now (CONTRACT.md, Trust profiles), for the first host of its connection string. Absent when the engine is down.

host.description: The host as the connection string names it.

applies.description: PROFILE: a trust profile's roots with the system's authorities. SSLROOTCERT: the roots the connection string names (sslrootcert, PGSSLROOTCERT, ~/.postgresql/root.crt). SYSTEM: the system's authorities alone. NOT_VERIFIED: sslmode is below verify-full, so the host name is not checked and no profile applies.

profile.description: The profile's name, when applies is PROFILE.

origin.description: BUILT_IN: embedded in this build. OPERATOR: a file in trust.d.

verify.description: CA: a pin that checks the chain against its own root alone, without the host name (verify: ca). Absent: the chain and the host name are checked.

rootCount.description: How many roots the profile holds.

roots.description: Up to 8 of the profile's roots, those that expire first.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the certificate's DER, uppercase hex pairs joined by colons.

engineRecord.description: CONTRACT.md, Direct transport and Version 33: this engine's key as the agent's database records it. Absent when the engine is down.

state.description: RECORDED: the agent's database records this engine's key and has not revoked it. NOT_RECORDED: it does not record it (no setup code carried it, or the key was rotated since). REVOKED: the person revoked it; the engine hands over long links for this agent and refuses its portal sessions. UNKNOWN: the guard is older than version 33, the key file is refused, or the record could not be read.

url.description: The engine address recorded with the key, when there is one.

recordedAt.description: When the key was recorded (RECORDED, REVOKED).

update.description: status.update. Present only when a newer BasaltDB release is out (CONTRACT.md, Update notice). Tell the person; never upgrade without their OK.

latest.description: The newest release the person may be offered.

security.description: True when a release newer than the running build is a security release.

message.description: Starts WARNING: or SECURITY UPDATE:. Relay it to the person.

problems.description: Empty when everything is ready. Errors first.

code.description: TRUST_ROOT_CHANGED (CONTRACT.md, Trust profiles, Pinning on first use): the agent's database is pinned and presents another certificate authority now; the message names both fingerprints, and the person accepts the new one with basalt trust pin, never automatically. TRUST_PIN_MISMATCH (WARNING): the ledger records another pin for the database's host and port than the engine's (no record is no problem). CERTIFICATE_NOT_VERIFIED, TRUST_ROOT_EXPIRING and TRUST_PROFILE_REFUSED (CONTRACT.md, Trust profiles): the agent's database presents a certificate that verifies against neither the system's authorities nor a trust profile (the message names the host; the person adds its CA with basalt trust add or names it with sslrootcert); a root of the profile that verifies the agent's database expires within 90 days or has expired; a file in trust.d was not loaded, one problem per file naming it and why (a refused file named after a built-in keeps that built-in off until it is fixed; any other changes nothing). PORTAL_MISMATCH (CONTRACT.md, CLI, basalt portal verify): the engine's daily check found the portal serving pages other than the ones this build embeds. DEV_LOCAL_PAGES (CONTRACT.md, Page origins): the engine.json devLocalPages development exception is on, so the pages are on the agent's machine. ENGINE_REVOKED (CONTRACT.md, Direct transport): the agent's database revoked this engine's key. DIRECT_NOT_SERVED (CONTRACT.md, Direct transport): the agent's database records an address for this engine, but directAddr is off, so a tunnel has nothing to forward to. LOCK_FILE_UNUSABLE (CONTRACT.md, On the engine, Lock files): the engine cannot open engine.json.lock or the agent's credential lock, so a finished setup is not written back. LEDGER_REINSTALLED (CONTRACT.md, Version 36): the ledger records that the guard was installed again and an engine set its pin of the old ledger aside; personMessage is the reinstall notice, to show the person as it is. PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE (CONTRACT.md, Plugins): an enabled plugin entry for this agent is not ready, so a wire.detect plugin fails the agent's requests to the AI provider closed until it is back or disabled. PLUGIN_NOT_TRUSTED (CONTRACT.md, Plugins): the engine refused to start a plugin entry for this agent because its signature, file hashes or file permissions failed, or, in service mode, an agent's OS user is in the engine's group. PLUGIN_AWAITING_APPROVAL, PLUGIN_APPROVAL_EXPIRED and PLUGIN_APPROVAL_MISMATCH (CONTRACT.md, Plugins, Plugin approvals at engine start): an entry that requires a passkey approval is withheld from this agent because no signed approval names it, its approval expired unsigned, or its signed approval does not match the installed copy or config (the message names the fields that differ). A withheld entry blocks none of the agent calls. PLUGIN_CONFIG_INVALID (CONTRACT.md, Plugins, Plugin changes while the engine runs): engine.json changed while the engine runs and its plugins cannot be read, so the engine applies no plugin change and every plugin keeps its state. PLUGIN_NOTICES_DROPPED (Planned; CONTRACT.md, Plugins, Notifier messages): an approval.deliver entry for this agent dropped notices in the last 24 hours; the message names the entry and how many, never what they were about. The agent's answers carried the links all along. For a connect-only setup (CONTRACT.md, Setup from your laptop, The engine and a connect-only code): CONFIRM_DATABASE: the engine collected the database's address and asks the person, through the agent, to confirm it before it logs in. DATABASE_REFUSED: the person said no; a new code is needed. DATABASE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_BOT: the setup ran, but the engine's machine cannot reach that database (a firewall allow-list, an IPv6-only host); the person runs the same link again with a reachable connection string. ADDRESS_INVALID: the address the connect service handed over breaks the engine's own address rules, so nothing of it is shown. SETUP_NOT_FOUND: after the person confirmed, the engine logged in but the database does not record its setup. CLOCK_SKEW: the connect service refused the engine's collect request because the engine's clock is more than 5 minutes off. ENGINE_AS_ROOT: the engine runs as root without --user, so it does not collect this agent's address; the engine's other agents are served as usual.

severity.description: ERROR: tools other than status do not work until it is fixed. WARNING: they work.

personMessage.description: The message the agent shows the person verbatim, keeping its line breaks; each URL on a line of its own (planned, M3.5) (CONTRACT.md, Showing links).

links.description: The URLs of personMessage with labels, in order; present exactly when personMessage holds a URL.
